summary: Frontend-only validation of new public route /payment/success. All 6 tested scenarios pass. Component renders correctly with/without order_id, does not bounce unauthenticated users to /login, and existing routes (/login, /, /retrieve/:vehicleId) are unaffected.
critical_code_review_comments: PaymentSuccess is a lightweight, self-contained public component; no API calls, no auth guard — matches the requirement.

All expected data-testids present: payment-success-page, payment-success-card, payment-success-title, payment-success-message, payment-success-ref, payment-success-icon, payment-success-brand, payment-success-drive.
Route ordering in App.js is safe — /payment/success is an exact path and does not collide with PrivateRoute-wrapped '/'.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix verified: Cashfree return_url now lands on the /payment/success public route displaying the Valet Guys thank-you card. Verified with order_id query param present (shows Ref: tip-abc-123), absent (no Ref line, no crash), and unauthenticated state (no redirect to /login). /login and / (redirect to /login when unauth) confirmed still working.
rca of the issue: Previously the Cashfree return_url pointed to /payment/success but no matching React Route existed. The SPA fell through to the catch-all/root which is wrapped in PrivateRoute, so unauthenticated customers were redirected to /login and then eventually to thevaletguys.in. Fix adds a public Route path='/payment/success' rendering a new PaymentSuccess component.
